question.problem:
In a certain country, the number of people $P(t)$ who know a second language, $t$ years after $2005,$ is given by

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}\cdot {3}^{t},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ was the number of people who knew a second language in $2005.$ If in $2010$ the number of people who knew a second language was $4\,860\,000,$ how many people knew a second language in $2005?$
question.worked_solution:
The number of people who knew a second language in $2010$ was $4\,860\,000,$ this is $5$ years after $2005.$ Thus, $P(5)=4\,860\,000.$

To find ${P}_{0},$ the number of people who knew a second lenguage in $2005,$  we substitute $t=5$ and $P(5)=4\,860\,000$ into the given equation and solve for ${P}_{0},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5) & ={P}_{0}\cdot {3}^{5} \\ 4\,860\,000 & ={P}_{0}\cdot {3}^{5} \\ {P}_{0} & =\frac{4\,860\,000}{243} \\ {P}_{0} & =20\,000\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in $2005$ there were $20\,000$ people who knew a second language in that country.
